source: YouTube auto-caption transcript 0:00-19:45 (tools/video_draft.py transcript I_Cdetq8Rhc --start 0 --end 1170), card names corrected against data/Sets/FRA_PremierDraft_All_Data.json; nothing past 19:45 read. 'type' marks each idea as claim, heuristic or one-off pick; 'repeats' lists ideas of earlier videos it restates; 'related' lists looser topic matches. Solo draft: every idea is the host's (speaker field kept for the schema).

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: Guiding Hydra is a card to first-pick nearly every time: better than basically every common and uncommon, and monocoloured; but not a card he loves splashing because it fits aggressive two-colour decks.
ideas.quote: Definitely a card that you should be first picking pretty much every time you see it in packs.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Guiding Hydra by skill group and by number of colours in the deck.

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: Mindseeker Oculus is an incredible common: every time you play it you feel you come out ahead.
ideas.quote: Just incredible common and just like every time you play this, you feel like you come out ahead.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Mindseeker Oculus.

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: Stingerquill Voxmancer is really bad: every time an opponent played it he won, because it is inefficient and spending the Vicious Verse feels bad.
ideas.quote: I think Stingerquil Voxmaner is really bad. Like every I feel like every time my opponent has played this card, I've won the game.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Stingerquill Voxmancer.

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: Solarium Sentry is incredible if you know you play white (a two-mana 3/3 that gains life), but picking it first of a pack with no mono-white follow-up is not worth losing flexibility.
ideas.quote: If I knew I was playing white, Solarium Sentry is incredible.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Solarium Sentry by colour pair; Sentry against No Admittance at P1p2.

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: Prefer the more flexible card early, so you can still abandon the first pick: No Admittance over Solarium Sentry; the cost of that approach is that it sometimes gets you wrecked.
ideas.quote: This card's more flexible and I could still abandon the guiding hydra if white doesn't end up being open. ... it ends up being a pretty like not good strategy for not getting like kind of wrecked here.
ideas.test_idea: Share of drafters who end in the colours of their P1p1 against their P1p2 pick.

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: Craterclaw Colossus is a card to build around at pick three, with Heartwood tokens, Afterthought Sentry and other artifacts; he picks it to learn about it.
ideas.quote: Pick three is a time when we could build around it. Put a couple extra artifacts in our deck. And it is interesting to get experience with these cards.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Craterclaw Colossus by artifact count.

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: Marwyn, the Preserver is the best card in a red-green-leaning pack, over the Wrecking Gecko, which he does not prioritise.
ideas.quote: I think Marwin is the best card in this pack.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Marwyn, the Preserver against Wrecking Gecko.

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: Seeing a strong gold card sixth (Jiang Yanggu, Never Alone) is a nice signal for red-green.
ideas.quote: Seeing one of these pick six is a nice little signal.
ideas.test_idea: Whether a Jiang Yanggu at P1p6 predicts red-green flow.

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: Arni, Renowned Champion is horrifically bad usually, and he does not want it even as a last-pick option.
ideas.quote: I don't want the Arie. Just think he's horrifically bad usually.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Arni, Renowned Champion.

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: Overwrite the Multiverse is one of the best bombs in the set, yet he does not take it: he plays red-green and passes it for Something Worth Saving to find the Colossus.
ideas.quote: Overwrite the multiverse is one of the best bombs in the set.
ideas.test_idea: How often a P2p1 bomb outside the drafter's colours reaches the deck.

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: Something Worth Saving is better in a deck with a payoff to find: every copy helps find the Colossus, so he takes it over random good cards.
ideas.quote: Every copy of this helps us find it more consistently over like these random cards that are pretty good but not as interesting.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Something Worth Saving by number of artifact payoffs in the deck.

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: The first copy of Murmuring Volume is much better than the second; mana rocks that give upside seem pretty decent.
ideas.quote: Feel like the first copy of this way better than the second.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Murmuring Volume by copy count.

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: Take removal over a second copy of a digging spell when removal is short: Fulminous Forte over Something Worth Saving.
ideas.quote: We do need extra removal and we already have a something worth saving.
ideas.test_idea: Marginal value of the second Something Worth Saving against a removal spell.

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: Craftwork Crusher is exactly the payoff he wants: an insane artifact that finishes games; he takes it over Bestial Incursion and a red-green land.
ideas.quote: This card's insane. It's another great payoff. It's an artifact and finding that more often is also going to be great for us.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Craftwork Crusher.

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: A pack of two-drops: with six two-drops already he stops taking them (Greenhouse Propagator over Sureshot Sower, Skilled Battlecarver as filler).
ideas.quote: We already have five two drops. Like this isn't the best two drop, but it's totally fine with our plan.
ideas.test_idea: Two-drop count against win rate in ramp decks.

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: A rare in your colours at pick one of pack three is like getting a rare for your deck: Craftwork Crusher over Lyra, Archangel of Dawn, and no need to splash white.
ideas.quote: This is like getting a rare for our deck.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Craftwork Crusher against Lyra, Archangel of Dawn.

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: Kiora of Fire and Ashes and the two Jiang Yanggus are 'uncommons that are just extra rares in our deck': the uncommons in this set play as rares.
ideas.quote: We have three uncommons that are just extra rares in our deck.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of the red-green uncommons against the rares of the set.

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: With 24 playables already, take the dual land to make the mana consistent (Konstrari Annex) over a third Improviser; he already has six two-drops.
ideas.quote: I'm tempted to just take the dual land, make my deck more consistent. This is red, red, green, green, after all.
ideas.test_idea: Play rate of Konstrari Annex in red-green decks.

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: He does not splash the Hydra even with Overgrown Farmland and Dedicated Commons available: splashing adds risk to a deck with so much top end that only has to survive and get there.
ideas.quote: I don't think we want to splash. Just seems risky.
ideas.test_idea: Win rate of the Hydra as a splash against its non-splash rate.

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: Twinned Vision helps avoid flood in a deck with many mana rocks and top end, but a second copy is not needed with filtering already.
ideas.quote: Twin Division again might not be the best in this deck because I already have a couple card filtering cards.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Twinned Vision in ramp decks.

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: With about 22 creatures and many seven-drops, cut the cheap and aggressive cards (Battlecarver, Hallway Heckler) and keep the top end: he is a midrange deck winning the late game.
ideas.quote: Battle Carver is much more of an aggressive card. I'm more of a mid-range like winning the late game.
ideas.test_idea: Average curve against win rate for ramp decks.

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: Do not cut a top-end card to make room: the Archive Arbiter is a seven-drop in this deck, not a six-drop, and he would rather cut an Afterthought Sentry and the Keeper.
ideas.quote: I might just cut the archive arbiter. These are seven drops though. These are not six drops.
ideas.test_idea: Top-end count (6+ mana) against win rate in ramp decks.

ideas.speaker: NicolaiBolas (host)
ideas.claim: A dual land taken highly pays off at the build: he was already going to struggle to make cuts, so the Konstrari Annex improves the mana without costing a spell.
ideas.quote: This is why I took this land so highly because I was already going to struggle to make cuts.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Konstrari Annex in RG decks.
